newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Foreign chambers wants lower Manila corporate tax.
newsitem.headline: Foreign chambers wants lower Manila corporate tax.

text.p: Six foreign chambers of commerce said on Wednesday that corporate income tax should be cut to 30 percent from 35 percent under the proposed Philippine tax reform package.
The position paper was drafted by the American, Australian-New Zealand, Canadian, European, Japanese and Korean chambers of commerce in the Philippines.
The House of Representatives approved last week the last part of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package on income taxes.
Among its key components are the tax exemption for families with an annual income of less than 146,000 pesos, but it maintained the corporate tax at 35 percent on net income.
The foreign chambers said the big increase in the exemption to taxpayers was not the correct approach to tax reforms since it would be made at the expense of discouraging investments.
"Every taxpayer should be made to feel that he or she has the duty to share in the financial burdens of government," the chambers said in a statement.

"To recover the revenue loss arising from the exemption from corporate taxpayers could be counter-productive and could discourage investments, whether domestic or foreign. It should be recognised that corporations are now burdened with so many taxes," they said.
The groups added that the bill's limits on foreign travel should be removed. The bill allows only 50 percent of the allowable foreign travel expenses as tax deductible.

"The chambers strongly support the government's desire to simplify tax administration... but they believe the real focus should be on the non-payment of taxes by those who are evading taxes," the groups said.
The Senate has yet to act on the proposed tax package.
The passage of the tax bill will ensure the exit of the Philippines from International Monetary Fund supervision.
